summary: 43 raster runs, almost all drawn as one full-frame raster over a context raster that the output completely hides, so input and output are rarely seen together; a render-only swipe curtain would lift a dozen entries at once. The best pictures are walking-cost (isochrone bands over Grand Canyon terrain), raster-reprojection (painted grid visibly rotated), polygon-rasterization and raster-join; the worst are fractional-coverage (unaligned bars over tract outlines), normalized-difference-water-index and make-raster-band (flat light-blue NDWI of a scene with no water), morphological-reconstruction (output looks exactly like the input terrain) and spectral-unmixing (default shows an auto-ranged residual of pure numerical noise). 14 runs scrub a Data: knob (or an unlabelled data knob such as 'Added noise', 'Tract boundary scale', 'Post-fire change multiplier') while several have spatial inputs already written per frame (walking-cost sources, watershed markers, raster-profile line positions, raster-sampling positions, make-raster-grid origin, raster-registration shift) that only need a 2D pointer binding. The four index runs (NBR, NDWI, SAVI, EVI) bind only compile-time numerical guards or data haze, and the Feather River reflectance extract is pre-fire land with no open water, so water and burn indices have nothing to show. The zone helper support/zones.ts samples a nearest-tract (piecewise constant) field, which makes per-zone std, min/max and quantiles degenerate in four zonal runs, and raster-zonal-statistics and fractional-zonal-statistics posters are near duplicates. uint32 label rasters wrap into 8 categorical colours, so sieve, patch-metrics, watershed, region-adjacency-graph and polygon-rasterization show neighbouring patches in the same colour. Shared fixes in support/zones.ts, support/patches.ts, support/bands.ts (drawRaster) and the reflectance extract would fix most quality problems.

sharedChanges.change: createZoneInputs.field is a nearest-tract-center assignment, so every tract covers nearly one constant value and zonal std, min/max, quantiles and class shares are degenerate; sample a continuous field instead (createSmoothField, the elevation raster, or an interpolated ACS surface) so within-zone distributions exist.

getPatchLabels emits up to 90 labels that the categorical ramp wraps into 8 colours, so adjacent patches share colours; add a helper that remaps labels to a greedy graph colouring by adjacency (or draw patch boundaries) for display only.

drawRaster is used for an input context layer that the output fully covers; once the framework has a swipe curtain, let drawRaster pairs declare {before, after} so each index/filter run gets input|output comparison in one line, and default sequential/diverging outputs to fixed ranges instead of 'auto'.

The Sentinel-2 extract is the Feather River on 2021-07-13 (pre-fire, no open water), so NDWI is uniformly slightly negative and NBR shows no burn; add a second extract with a reservoir (e.g. Lake Almanor) and a post-fire date of the same footprint, recorded in THIRD-PARTY-DATA.md, so water and burn indices have a subject.

fill-holes, medial-axis and skeleton all threshold the same 72-row elevation raster at 0.5, leaving a small shape in the top-right corner; a shared binary-shape helper with a centered, ~40% land mask (or a hydrography lake/river polygon) would fill the frame and let a pointer stamp edit the mask.

pointer to world/cell mapping passed to update(values, pointer) so a run can write a pointer-driven buffer (source cell, marker, seed, stamp, line endpoint) without inventing a fake slider
2D pointer binding to two parameters (x and y), not only one cardScrub parameter
pointer glyphs: crosshair, ring of radius r (world units), axis-aligned box of (2r+1) cells, line from anchor to pointer, arrow by angle
highlight buffer for raster cells and for polygons (hovered zone id -> emphasized fill/outline), driven by a per-frame uint32 id
pointer to polygon id lookup (point-in-polygon on CPU tract rings) and pointer to raster label lookup
readback of one or a few buffer values at the hovered cell or zone for the readout chip (value, class, fraction)
small per-cell inset chart fed from CPU arrays or a readback (time series with a split line, bar of band values, scatter with regression line)
pre-built variants for compile-time props (build N graphs once, switch per frame) with debounce for continuous snapped values
categorical legend and fixed category colours for small class sets (significance increase/decrease/none, majority class)
chart references: identity diagonal on a LUT line chart, axes/frames on inset charts
